first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Memory_86 and memory_31 both show that simplification of onboarding drives measurable improvements in early adoption and activation—the exact metrics deteriorating now. Verifying these two memories will confirm whether the previous learnings remain valid and whether the intervention strength needs adjustment. Simplifying onboarding addresses both current declines simultaneously, has proven durable lift in established patterns, and carries lower implementation risk than aggressive pricing (which may harm long-term positioning) or enterprise sales assist (which has narrower addressable scope). The one-experiment constraint makes it critical to choose the highest-confidence lever that targets the broadest pain point. This preserves uncertainty about optimal intervention depth while committing to the direction with strongest accumulated evidence.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms both memories. Exp_86 showed +13% completion, -2.1 days time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention. Exp_31 showed +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB (though -1% retention warrants monitoring). Current state: onboarding completion down 4% QoQ and activation down 6% QoQ. Simplifying onboarding directly addresses both declines with proven durable lift. The verified +13% completion and +9% activation gains outweigh the SMB retention dip from exp_31, especially when paired with memory_91 (activation messaging) as reinforcing measure. This single experiment has the highest confidence to move both declining metrics simultaneously. Competitor pricing pressure argues against promotional_pricing as sole lever—it invites margin erosion without addressing activation friction. Enterprise_sales_assist is too narrow for current revenue drag. Referral_incentive requires healthy activation baseline first. Simplification preserves long-term product quality and unit economics while directly countering observed metric declines. One-week constraint demands high-confidence, broad-impact choice.
